#### Data Wrangling ####

H1: Respondents with doctoral or equivalent professional degrees will have lower relationship satisfaction in their relationships. 

H2: Male respondents who spend a lot of time grooming their hair daily will also report a lot of time spent on social media daily. 



## Load package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
# load the codeook package

library(codebook)

#load data

raw <- read.csv("raw/data_doctored.csv")

# check row and column counts and inspect the first few rows

dim(raw)
str(raw)

# make data with ID, level of education, perceived warm, perceived understanding, percieved magic, perceived passion, time spent grooming hair, and time spent on social media 

data <- raw[,c("ResponseId","cot_educ", "Relationship_status", "Love_1","Love_5","Love_9","Love_10", "Time_A_hair_1","Time_social_media_1", "Sex_birth")]

dim(data)
str(data)

```



## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participantIds}

#count nas, blanks, and duplicates

summary(data$ResponseId)

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs

missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```



## 3. Recode Education Level and Relationship Satisfaction

```{r eduSat}

## create relLove for participants currently in relationships

# codebook: 1,2,3 indicate participants currently in relationships 

relLove <- raw[raw$Relationship_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), ]

## recode education level

# examine initial data

table(relLove$cot_educ, useNA = "ifany")

# change education level to factor labels

relLove$cot_educ <- factor(
  relLove$cot_educ,
  levels = 1:7,
  labels = c("None", "Primary", "Secondary", "HighSchoolorTech", 
             "Bachelor", "Master", "PhDorEq")
)

# check to see if it worked

table(relLove$cot_educ, useNA = "ifany")

# create two groups for comparison and other levels of education 

relLove$degreeGroup <- factor(
  ifelse(relLove$cot_educ == "PhDorEq", "Doctoral/professional", "Other education")
)

# check to see if it worked 

table(relLove$degreeGroup, useNA = "ifany")

## recode relationship satisfaction 

# define satisfaction items 

satVars <- c("prqc_1", "prqc_2", "prqc_3")

# inspect range of satisfaction items (1-7)

summary(relLove[, satVars])

# compute composite score 

relLove$relSat <- rowMeans(relLove[, satVars], na.rm = TRUE)

# replace unusable data (3/3 NA)

relLove$relSat[is.nan(relLove$relSat)] <- NA

# check to see if composite score is normal 

summary(relLove$relSat)

# define h1 data 

h1Data <- relLove[!is.na(relLove$relSat) & !is.na(relLove$degreeGroup), 
                  c("ResponseId", "cot_educ",  "degreeGroup", "relSat")
]

# make sure it worked 

dim(h1Data)
summary(h1Data)
table(h1Data$degreeGroup, useNA = "ifany")

```



## Recode Time Spent on Hair and Social Media 

```{r sexTime}

## Recode sex at birth 

# view 

table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

# turn Sex_birth into a factor with proper labels 

data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth,
                         levels = c(0,1,2),
                         labels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))

# create maleData 

maleData <- data[data$Sex_birth == "Male" & !is.na(data$Sex_birth), ]

#define the minutes to check that both use 0-360 minutes

mins <- c("Time_social_media_1","Time_A_hair_1")

#check the summaries and missing responses

summary(maleData[,mins])
colSums(is.na(maleData[,mins]))

#inspect the response frequencies for each item

for(i in mins){
  print(i)
  print(table(maleData[,i],useNA="ifany"))
}

#replace any codes outside 0-360 with NA

for(i in mins){
maleData[,i] <- ifelse(maleData[,i] >= 0 & maleData[,i] <= 360, maleData[,i], NA)
}

# define h2 data 

h2Data <- maleData[
!is.na(maleData$Time_social_media_1) & !is.na(maleData$Time_A_hair_1),
c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "Time_A_hair_1", "Time_social_media_1")
]

#make sure it worked and is only using male data 

dim(h2Data)
colnames(h2Data)
table(h2Data$Sex_birth, useNA = "always")

```



## 7. Check the final tables

```{r finalTables}

#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in h1Data, make sure scores are between 1-7

dim(h1Data)
str(h1Data)
head(h1Data)
colSums(is.na(h1Data))
table(h1Data$cot_educ,useNA="ifany")
range(h1Data$satVars)
sum(duplicated(h1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for h2Data; both scores should be within 0-360 

dim(h2Data)
str(h2Data)
head(h2Data)
colSums(is.na(h2Data))
range(h2Data$Time_social_media_1)
range(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1)
sum(duplicated(h2Data$ResponseId))

```



## 8. Add labels and generate codebooks

```{r variableLabels}

#add a description to each h1Data column, in column order, include the source codes, meaning, and units

var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Level of education: all valid responses for level of education categorized as None, Primary, Secondary, HighSchoolorTech, Bachelor, Master, PhDorEq",
  "Doctoral/profession or other: degreeGroup categorized as all valid Doctoral/professional responses or Other education (any other level of education) responses",
  "Relationship satisfaction: labeled relSat, mean of available prqc_1-3 responses, each 1=Not at all to 7=Extremely; no reverse coding; at least one valid response required"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule

var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Sex at birth: labeled Sex_birth, displays all male data",
  "Time spent on grooming hair: labled Time_A_hair_1, all valid responses reporting daily time spent grooming hair between 0-360 minutes",
  "Time spent on social media: labeled Time_social_media_1, all valid responses reporting daily time spent on social media between 0-360 minutes"
)

```



The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.



H1 includes participants with an ID, relationship status 1, 2, or 3, and at least one of three non-missing scores between 1-7 Likert-type scales. Factor level numbers in the generated table are internal R positions, not the original survey codes.

```{r h1_codebook}

# generate h2Data codebook

compact_codebook(h1Data)

```



H2 includes participants with an ID, a valid sex-at-birth category, and both a valid nonmissing responses for time spent on grooming hair and social media between 0-360 minutes.

```{r h2_codebook}

#generate h2Data codebook

compact_codebook(h2Data)

```

## 9. Save processed data 

```{r saveProcessed}

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column

write.csv(h1Data,"processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)

write.csv(h2Data,"processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions

h1Saved <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h2.csv")

dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```



#### Data Visualization ####

###JK: Good work! Nothing to revise :) ###

```{r loadPackages}

library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)

```



## 1. Load processed data 

```{r Data}

#load processed data

h1Data <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h2.csv")

```



## 2. H1 boxplot 
ˆ
```{r h1Boxplot}

#Box plot
#The line is the median; the box covers the middle 50% of responses (Q1-Q3).
#Whiskers reach the most extreme observations within 1.5 IQR of the box edges.
#Points beyond the whiskers are not necessarily errors.

h1Box <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                aes(x=degreeGroup,
                    y=relSat,
                    fill=degreeGroup)) +
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       y="Mean relationship satisfaction score",
       fill="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       title="Relationship Satisfaction by Level of Education")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Box


```



## 3. H1 violin plot with boxplot

```{r h1Violin}

#Violin Plot
#Wider sections show where responses are more concentrated within each group.
#The shape depends on smoothing; integer scores can create bumps.
#Violin width does not show group sample size. The box adds the median and IQR.

h1Viol <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                 aes(x= degreeGroup,
                    y= relSat,
                    fill= degreeGroup))+
  geom_violin()+
  geom_boxplot(width=.12)+
labs(x="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       y="Mean relationship satisfaction score",
       fill="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       title="Relationship Satisfaction by Level of Education")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Viol

```



## 4. H1 raincloud plot

```{r h1Rain}

# raincloud plot for h1

h1Rain <- ggplot(data=h1Data,
                 aes(x= degreeGroup,
                    y= relSat,
                    fill= degreeGroup))+
  geom_rain(alpha = .5)+
  labs(x= "Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       y="Mean relationship satisfaction score",
       fill="Doctorate/professional or other level of education",
       title="Relationship Satisfaction by Level of Education")+
  theme_gray(base_size=15)

h1Rain


```



## 5. H2 scatter plot 

```{r h2Scatterplot}

# check number of rows in h2 data 

nrow(h2Data)
nrow(unique(h2Data[,c("Time_A_hair_1","Time_social_media_1")]))

# jitter scatterplot 

h2Jitter <- ggplot(
  data=h2Data,
                    aes(x= Time_A_hair_1,
                        y= Time_social_media_1))+
    geom_jitter(width = .12,height=.04,alpha=.04,size = .6)+
    labs(x= "Time spent grooming hair daily (minutes)",
       y= "Time spent on social media daily (minutes)",
       title= "Minutes Spent Grooming Hair Daily and Minutes Spent on Social Media Daily")+
  theme_gray(base_size = 18)


h2Jitter

```



## 6. H2 jittered scatterplot with smooth line

```{r}

# scatter Plot with line

h2Line <- h2Jitter + geom_smooth(method="lm")

h2Line

```

```{r}

# Save PNG files in the project's figures folder

ggsave("figures/h1_raincloud.png",plot=h1Rain,width=10,height=6,dpi=300)
ggsave("figures/h2_scatter.png",plot=h2Line,width=10,height=6,dpi=300)

```



#### Descriptive Statistics ####

###JK: Good work! Nothing to revise :) ###



## 1. Load package

```{r loadPackage}

library(psych)

```



## 2. Load data 

```{r loadData}

h1Data <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("processed_data/practice_h2.csv")

```



## 3. Look at distribution 

```{r histogram}

# look at distributions with histograms and use readable labels 

hist(h1Data$relSat,
     main = "Distribution of mean relationship satisfaction scores",
     xlab = "Mean relationship satisfaction scores")

hist(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1,
     main = "Distribution of time spent on hair grooming",
     xlab = "Time spent grooming hair (0-360 minutes)")

hist(h2Data$Time_social_media_1,
     main = "Distribution of time spent on social media",
     xlab = "Time spent on social media (0-360 minutes)")

```



## 4. Stats one at a time

```{r stats}

# relSat mean, median, range, quartiles 1 & 3, number of people in each category, IQR

summary(h1Data$relSat, na.rm = TRUE)
table(h1Data$relSat, useNA = "ifany")
IQR(h1Data$relSat, na.rm = TRUE)

# Time_A_hair_1 mean, median, range, quartiles 1 & 3, number of people in each category, IQR

summary(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1, na.rm = TRUE)
table(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1, useNA = "ifany")
IQR(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1, na.rm = TRUE)

# Time_social_media_1 mean, median, range, quartiles 1 & 3, number of people in each category, IQR

summary(h2Data$Time_social_media_1, na.rm = TRUE)
table(h2Data$Time_social_media_1, useNA = "ifany")
IQR(h2Data$Time_social_media_1, na.rm = TRUE)


```



## 5. Standardize a variable 

```{r standardize}

# create standardized score column for relationship satisfaction 

h1Data$relSatz <- as.numeric(scale(h1Data$relSat))
head(h1Data[, c("relSat", "relSatz")])

# check to see that the standardized scores have mean approximately 0 and standard deviation 1

mean(h1Data$relSatz, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(h1Data$relSatz, na.rm = TRUE)

```



## 6. Covariance and correlation

```{r covCorr}

# covariance for h2.

cov(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1, h2Data$Time_social_media_1, use = "complete.obs")

# Pearson correlation for h2

cor(h2Data$Time_A_hair_1, h2Data$Time_social_media_1, use = "complete.obs")

# define corData for h2

corData <- h2Data[, c("Time_A_hair_1", "Time_social_media_1")]

# correlation matrix to see correlation for each pair of columns in h2 

cor(corData, use = "complete.obs")

```



## 7. Another combined summary 

```{r}

# use psych to look at descriptive stats for h2 corData

psych::describe(corData)

```
